textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 english · Three Days to See · Chapter Map
textbookBox.concept: Think of a place you loved visiting. What did you see there? What did you hear and smell? Now imagine that you could not see or hear. Our five senses help us experience and make sense of the world.

textbookBox.concept: You recall a visit to a place you liked, write its name, who you went with, and what you could see, then think how it would feel and be different if you could not see or hear.

beats.en: Helen Keller finds hundreds of things to interest her through touch alone. She feels the delicate symmetry of a leaf, the smooth skin of a silver birch and the rough, shaggy bark of a pine.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 english · Three Days to See · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: She would divide her three days into three parts. On the first day she would see the people whose kindness and companionship have made her life worth living. She calls the eye the window of the soul.

beats.en: She would divide her three days into three parts. On the first day she would see the people whose kindness and companionship have made her life worth living. She calls the eye the window of the soul.
beats.speakEn: She would divide her three days into three parts. On the first day she would see the people whose kindness and companionship have made her life worth living. She calls the eye the window of the soul.

beats.en: On the second day she would rise at dawn and watch the thrilling miracle of night turning into day, and the magnificent panorama of light with which the sun awakens the sleeping earth.
